newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to woo Kuwait investment after pact signed.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to woo Kuwait investment after pact signed.

text.p: Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa said on Sunday his country expected to attract Kuwaiti investment and to enter new markets in the Middle and Far East, the state news agency HINA said.
Matesa spoke after returning from a two-day visit to Kuwait in which he signed a bilateral agreement on investment promotion and protection.
His Kuwait trip came on the heels of a visit to Malaysia and Indonesia aimed at boosting trade and attracting their investments to Croatia, a former Yugoslav republic.
"This is part of an effort by the Croatian government and Chamber of Economy to find new markets so to expand the horizons of the Croatian economy," Matesa told HINA.
Some 80 percent of Croatian foreign trade is conducted with Germany, Italy, Austria and Slovenia. Trade between Kuwait and Croatia has so far amounted to a meagre $200,000 a year.

"We also want to ensure new investments in Croatia on the basis of lucrative and long-term cooperation. I think we found this in all three cases," Matesa said, referring to Kuwait, Malaysia and Indonesia.

Croatia owes $200 million to Kuwait inherited as a part of former Yugoslavia's foreign debt after the country broke up in 1991. The talks between Croatia and Kuwait focused on converting the debt into joint investments, HINA said.
"We are very satisfied with the results of the talks we had. These investmens will happen very soon in the shape of well-defined projects," Matesa said.
Projects should be finalised in the area of infrastructure, tourism and construction like the building of a business centre in Zagreb and investments in hotels on the Adriatic coast.
A Kuwaiti delegation should visit Zagreb in April to initial these agreements, HINA said.
Kuwait also showed interest in processing Kuwaiti oil in Croatia's biggest refinery in the port of Rijeka and for acquiring a stake in the Adriatic pipeline Janaf.
Vanja Kalogjera, head of Croatia's Agency for Investment Promotion, told HINA that Kuwait could also invest a fresh $250 million in the Croatian economy.

The visit of Matesa's delegation could also renew the sale of Croatian military industry products to Kuwait. When it was still part of Yugoslavia, Croatia supplied Kuwait with M-84 tanks which now need servicing, HINA said.
